resources.string: Not linked. Calls ring only on this phone.
Linked to %1$s (%2$s), %3$s.\nYour carrier shows a message to confirm. Tap “Check with carrier” if you are not sure.
Request sent to your carrier. Wait for its confirmation message.
When to send calls to the other phone
Only if unanswered (use this if your carrier rejects the first option)
All calls, without ringing this phone
Ask your carrier, or leave empty
Linking replaces your carrier’s “send to voicemail” setting. With this number, unlinking puts voicemail back. Without it, unlinking turns forwarding off completely.
Allow the other phone to link or unlink this one
For when you left this phone behind. Install Phone Link on both phones, set the same PIN on both, and turn this on for both. Only SMS from the other phone’s number with the right PIN are accepted.
PIN (4–8 digits, the same on both phones)
SMS sent. You will be notified when the other phone answers.
Other phone: linked. Its calls will come to you.
Other phone could not reach its carrier. Open Phone Link on it to check permissions.
Other phone rejected the PIN. Use the same PIN on both phones.
A remote request with a wrong PIN was ignored.
A remote request was ignored because remote control is off.
Tip: add the “Phone Link” tile to your Quick Settings (swipe down, then tap the pencil) to link or unlink in one tap.
Enter the other phone’s number first.
This is not a valid phone number.
The PIN must have 4 to 8 digits.
Allow Phone Link to make calls; it needs this to send codes to your carrier.
This device cannot make phone calls.
The SMS could not be sent.
Tip: with two different carriers, write the number in international format (+…) to be safe.

Android blocks SMS permissions for apps installed from outside the Play Store. To allow them: open Settings → Apps → Phone Link, tap ⋮ (top right) → “Allow restricted settings”, then turn remote control on again.
Send an alert to my other phone (free)
Forward calls through my carrier (may be billed)

While linked, every call ringing on this phone is announced on your other phone within a second or two, with the caller’s name and a “Call back” button. On the other phone, install the free ntfy app and subscribe to the topic below.
Not allowed yet. Phone Link needs to be your “caller ID & spam” app to see incoming calls. It never blocks or silences a call.
This creates a new random topic. The other phone stops receiving alerts until you subscribe it to the new topic. Use this if someone else may know your topic.
Anyone who knows this name can read your alerts, so keep it random and private.
If there’s no internet, send an SMS instead
Uses the other phone’s number above. Your plan may charge for SMS.
Test alert sent. It should appear on your other phone now.
The alert could not be sent. Check the internet connection and the ntfy server.
Install ntfy on the other phone

The ntfy app is not installed on this phone. Alerts are received by the OTHER phone: install ntfy there, tap +, and subscribe to:

Server: %1$s
Topic: %2$s
Alerts on, %1$s.\nCalls ringing on this phone are announced on your other phone.
Alerts on. Calls on this phone will be announced on the other one.
Enter a server address starting with https://
The topic may only contain letters, digits, - and _ (up to 64).
Your carrier sends unanswered calls to the other phone so you can pick them up there. Forwarded minutes are often billed as outgoing calls from this phone.
